tasks.goal: Implement controller-death recovery for previously observed nested worker descendants from design/controller-death-nested-processes-v1.md. Extend ManagedWorkerProcess with a bounded exact-identity external-descendant observer that replays its current snapshot on subscribe and emits changed snapshots from validated process-table samples; it must never signal. Extend backward-compatible WorkerLease version 1 with optional all-or-nothing nestedProcesses evidence containing version, host, observedCount, truncated, lastObservedAt and at most 32 deduplicated exact pid/pgid/os-start identities. The attacher must subscribe only after the immutable controller and worker identities are durably written, serialize atomic 0600 updates, never let an older snapshot overwrite a newer one, and fail closed by stopping/rejecting the invocation if nested-evidence persistence becomes unhealthy. A missing field must preserve legacy behavior; malformed, partial, duplicate or host-mismatched evidence must reject the lease. Extend recover-workers so a proven-dead controller can recover when the top-level leader is gone but a durable nested identity remains: never signal without exact identity, refresh a live top-level leader's descendant graph before group cleanup, recursively extend each matching nested root through the bounded process-table snapshot, fail closed before signalling on truncation, malformation, snapshot ambiguity or over-bound targets, persist the refreshed target set before signals, then TERM/SIGKILL exact nested pids only and verify they are gone. If the top-level leader is still exactly present, preserve the existing guarded dedicated-group cleanup; absence of the top-level leader never authorizes a negative-pgid signal. Expose bounded nested registry presence/count/truncation observation in WorkerLease status JSON without changing RunManifest acceptance. Add focused fake-inspector and real POSIX SIGKILL tests in the existing files for observer replay/update, durable nested persistence, write-failure rejection, truncated no-signal behavior, top-level-leader-absent nested recovery, exact-pid TERM/KILL, reused-pid refusal, legacy parsing and no orphan helpers. Do not change TaskContract, RunManifest authority, RuntimeManager, ports, Windows parity, cross-host recovery, automatic resume or RunManifest rewriting.
nonGoals: Do not implement OS filesystem or network sandboxing.
Do not add Windows Job Object support or cross-host recovery.
Do not use process names, ports, broad scans or negative-pgid signals without the existing exact leader guard.
Do not change TaskContract acceptance or rewrite RunManifest history.
Do not add a daemon or automatic resume.
